lines.text: Breitturm is at the point where the arrangements are sufficient and nothing is spare. One more demand on them and the town would be choosing which pressure to leave uncovered.
The town has no hill and no narrows and does not pretend otherwise; what Breitturm holds it holds by standing on it.
Very little reaches Breitturm out of the wild country, and the reason is that the arrangements are visible from a long way off.

lines.poolKey: Invasion & War: walls AND professional garrison
lines.text: A stranger sizing Breitturm up sees the two things that matter together (the wall and the men who belong to it) and revises what an attempt would cost.

lines.poolKey: Internal Security: full legal chain (court AND prison)
lines.text: A thing done wrong at Breitturm goes somewhere and takes time, and the town has come to rely on that rather than on the watch's temper.
The town's capacity to pay for its own emergencies is real and finite, and every season of pressure moves the finite part closer.

lines.poolKey: Disasters & Famine: granary AND parish care only
lines.text: There is food stored at Breitturm and there are clergy who tend the sick: reserves against hunger, and against disease something better than nothing and well short of a hospital.
There is a line around Breitturm and it is kept: the gates shut, the works are repaired, and a stranger enters where the town intends him to.
The soldiers at Breitturm belong to the town rather than to a season; they are a fixture, with all the friction and all the reliability of one.
A stranger at Breitturm finds a hall whose business is the sort of trouble a garrison is the wrong instrument for, and finds it busy.
Nothing unseen has come at Breitturm, and nothing here would know if it had; the record of safety and the capacity to detect are two different things.

lines.poolKey: COMPOUND override (a crisis stress has rewritten the label)
lines.text: Order at Breitturm is being held under a pressure the town's arrangements were not built for, and how long it holds is a question about the pressure rather than about the watch.

lines.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
lines.text: This is what Breitturm looks like on a first pass; a season here would either confirm it or correct it, and nobody has spent the season yet.

lines.poolKey: Logistics & Supply: Granary with road supply
lines.text: An interruption on the roads to Breitturm does not reach the table, and the granary is the reason rather than the roads.
The town walls around Breitturm is sound and the muster behind it is thinning, which is the kind of arithmetic a town notices late.
What Breitturm's defenses are ordinarily worth does not describe the town at present; there is a crisis on it, and the arrangements have been rebuilt around the crisis.
The crisis at Breitturm has changed the posture and not the prospects, and the town has been careful to keep the two separate.
Nothing structural at Breitturm depends on arcane work. What the town makes it makes with hands and ground, and would go on making without a practitioner in it.
Breitturm is on the way to somewhere and has made a modest living out of being on the way.
Breitturm keeps no market worth the name; exchange here happens at doorsteps and in yards, at the scale the town actually needs.

lines.poolKey: the MARGINAL arm: neither verdict returned
lines.text: Whether Breitturm holds together is not a settled question. The pieces mostly fit, and the places where they do not are the places worth reading.
What follows is Breitturm as it was judged when it was described, which is not the same as Breitturm as it stands.
Breitturm was never founded so much as agreed to, one household at a time.
Breitturm accepts the Guild Council without approving of it. The town's obedience is a habit rather than a verdict, and both sides understand the difference perfectly.
What the Guild Council has lost at Breitturm it has lost to the crime returns. A town that does not feel safe stops crediting whoever is meant to keep it so.

lines.poolKey: no token matched: unclassified (the plain-description floor)
lines.text: A stranger at Breitturm is directed to Guild Council for anything official, and that is all a stranger is told.
Nobody at Breitturm needs the trouble explained to them; it is recent enough that the town simply refers to it and moves on.
There is criminal infrastructure at Breitturm with local weight, territorial or economic, and no clearer description of it than that.

lines.poolKey: legitimacyHold: public opinion neither helps nor hurts
lines.text: The Guild Council at Breitturm is carrying its own weight and no more; a shift in the town's regard in either direction would be felt immediately, because there is nothing else cushioning the grip.

lines.poolKey: governing body name: a SLOT, never a baked noun
lines.text: What governs Breitturm calls itself the Guild Council, and the name is precise about the town's size and pretensions in a way outsiders routinely mistake.
There are interests at Breitturm and there are no camps; a question is answered by whoever cares about that question.
There is nothing striking about Breitturm's condition in either direction: a working road, a working market, a town neither building nor selling off.
People here put things by, and can. That is the difference between this town and a poorer one.
Breitturm is fed and only just comfortably. The margin is real and thin enough that a good season and a poor one feel different.

lines.poolKey: INCOME MIX: two or three sources between them
lines.text: Ask what this town lives on and you will be given a short list rather than an answer.

lines.poolKey: TRADE PROFILE: exports and imports both present
lines.text: The market at Breitturm carries the town's own goods and other towns' goods on the same stalls, and does not distinguish them for a stranger's benefit.
There is some thieving and some selling without a licence. Every town this size has both.
Breitturm sits on ground that grows things without argument, and the town's whole arrangement follows from that one fact.

lines.poolKey: ECONOMIC STRENGTHS: the roster is populated
lines.text: Breitturm has more than one thing it is good at, and the list is short enough that everybody here could recite it.

lines.poolKey: STRATEGIC VALUE: the generator's assessment, framed
lines.text: The town knows what it sits on, and knows that knowing is not the same as being able to keep it.
A stranger tracing wool out of Breitturm finds it leaving half-finished, and finds nobody in the town troubled by that.
Minor shadow activity. Petty theft and small-scale unlicensed trade. An inconvenience, not a structural threat.
